title: Rise of Andean civilization
summary: In the Initial Formative period, from 3000 to 1800 BCE, the Sacred City of Caral and 24 other centres with monumental architecture rose in coastal Peru. Researchers there call this the earliest civilization of the Americas. Its settlements had public buildings and sunken circular plazas. Scholars debate how far it rested on rich coastal fisheries, with farming added later.

uncertainty.note: Scientific Reports (Huamán et al. 2023) dates the Initial Formative / Caral urban complex to 3000–1800 BCE; Encyclopedia.com dates the Late Archaic Caral civilization to 3000–2000 BCE.

where.modern_name: Sacred City of Caral-Supe, Barranca Province, Lima Department, Peru
where.historical_name: Caral, Supe Valley (central ceremonial and urban center of the Caral-Supe civilization)

importance.justification: The Caral-Supe civilization represents the earliest pristine center of civilization in the Americas, pioneering Andean monumental architecture, urban spatial planning, and quipu record-keeping.

related.because: The Sacred City of Caral in the Supe Valley serves as the type site and primary urban center of early Andean civilization.
Earlier agricultural domestications in the Andes provided the dietary foundation for subsequent sedentary population growth.

sources.title: Analysis of starch grains trapped in human dental calculus in Áspero, Peru during the Initial Formative Period (3000-1800 BCE)
sources.publisher: Scientific Reports (Springer Nature, via PubMed Central)
sources.author: Pedro M. Huamán et al.

reviewer_note: The claim of earliest civilization comes partly from the team working at Caral. The pin marks Caral. Later Andean states have their own records.
